guard: completion resolves the command word as dispatch does, by exact name or alias, and offers names for a prefix rather than selecting one; a seeded package must claim the words its seed entry declares, aliases included
why: A <TAB> after an alias must complete inside that alias's command, or completion and dispatch disagree about what a word means.

The dispatcher resolves a seeded package's words before the first seed installs it, so an alias the entry does not declare would be an unknown command on a fresh machine. The check lives in the workspace package, which the suite imports through its build, so that mutation rebuilds it and the restore rebuilds it back.

mutations.name: completion resolves commands by name only
the seed check compares command names only
mutations.expectRed: an undeclared alias of a seeded command passed the seed check
mutations.cell: an undeclared alias of a seeded command passed the seed check
